title: Cloud Wants Colours
summary: Cloud is a white cloud, and she wants to be colourful like everything she sees down below. Until some rain teaches her where rainbows come from.

scenes.text:
High up, very high up, lived a small round cloud called Cloud.

From up there she could see everything. The red rooftops of the village. The yellow fields. The green trees, the purple flowers, the blue river.

Everything had colour.

Everything except her.

"How boring it is to be white!" Cloud sighed. "I want to be colourful too."

And that very day, she decided to get some colours.

First she tried the sunset.

She let the breeze carry her to where the sun was going down, and sat right on top of it. And it worked! She turned orange. Then pink. Then a beautiful gold.

But the sun went down. And Cloud was white again. Well, a little bit grey.

Then she saw something on top of a hill. It was a girl called Rosa, painting with watercolours. She had a palette full of colours and a jar of water.

Cloud floated gently down until she was right beside her.

"Excuse me," she said. "Could I borrow your paints?"

Rosa stared at her with her mouth open. Then she handed her the fattest brush she had.

Cloud painted her tummy pink. She painted her edges yellow. She gave herself an orange stripe and a green one. The brush tickled, and she couldn't stop the giggles.

"Look at me!" she shouted. "I'm colourful!"

But clouds are made of water. And with all that paint, and all that wet brush, Cloud got heavier. And heavier.

Until she couldn't hold on any longer.

And she began to rain.

She rained on the hill, on Rosa and on her sketchbook.

And with every drop, Cloud's colours washed away. The pink, the yellow, the orange, the green. Drop by drop, the water took them.

Cloud was white again. White and sad.

"They've gone," she cried. "They've all gone."

But just then, behind Cloud, the sun came out. And its rays shone through the last few drops.

And across the sky, from one side to the other, appeared a rainbow. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple.

"Cloud!" shouted Rosa. "Look! You did that!"

Cloud couldn't believe it.

Nobody had lent her those colours. They didn't come from the sunset, or from Rosa's paints.

They were hers. They had been there all along, hidden inside her drops, waiting for a ray of sunshine.

Since that day, Cloud doesn't mind being white.

Because she knows that every time it rains while the sun is shining, she paints the whole sky.

And in her sketchbook, Rosa keeps a drawing: a white cloud, smiling, with every colour in the sky spilling out of her tummy.
